_partNote: Four of the seven classes are aircraft, so they are separated by planform and scale cues rather than by role: a small X-shaped quadcopter, a twin-boom pusher with a rectangular wing on low gear, a large glider-proportioned aircraft with a V-tail on tall gear, and a slim cross-winged missile body. The remaining three change domain outright, with a low slender boat hull, a smooth torpedo body on saddle supports, and a squat tracked chassis. The loitering munition and the underwater vehicle are the closest pair, so the munition keeps four cross wings at midbody and the underwater vehicle is explicitly unbroken along its length with a ducted tail propeller.

partPrompts.1: A small quadcopter drone resting on its landing feet, seen three-quarter: a compact flat body with four straight arms spread in an X, each arm ending in a small two-blade rotor, and a small round camera ball hanging under the nose. Low, wide and flat, with the X plan the identifying geometry. No wings, no fuselage, no tail, no nose or tail propeller and no landing gear legs.
partPrompts.2: A twin-boom tactical uncrewed aircraft standing on low tricycle landing gear, seen three-quarter: a short stubby fuselage under a straight rectangular high wing, with two slender tail booms running back from the wing to a single horizontal tailplane joined between two upright fins, and one pusher propeller at the back of the fuselage between the booms. The twin booms and the plain rectangular wing are what must read. No V-tail, no rotors, no swept wing, no cockpit windows.
partPrompts.3: A large runway-based uncrewed aircraft standing on tall tricycle landing gear, seen three-quarter: a long slender fuselage with a bulged rounded nose, very long slim tapered wings spanning far wider than the fuselage is long, a downward-canted V-tail, and a single pusher propeller behind the tail. Big and glider-like in proportion, clearly the largest aircraft shape. No tail booms, no twin fins, no rotors, no cockpit windows.
partPrompts.4: A tube-launched loitering munition lying on a low stand, seen three-quarter: a slim cylindrical airframe with a blunt rounded nose, four short straight wings deployed in a cross around the middle of the body, four smaller fins in a cross at the tail, and a small two-blade propeller at the very back. Thin and missile-like. No landing gear, no launch tube, no boat hull, no rotors and no fuselage windows.
partPrompts.5: An uncrewed surface vessel hull sitting on a boat cradle, seen three-quarter: a long low slender monohull with a sharp raked bow, a flat clear deck running its whole length with no cabin or superstructure, and one short mast near the bow carrying a small sensor pod. The hull line is the silhouette. No windows, no railings, no crew, no water, no wake, no wings and no wheels.
partPrompts.6: A torpedo-shaped uncrewed underwater vehicle resting on two saddle supports, seen three-quarter: a smooth cylindrical body with a blunt rounded nose, a low rounded fairing on top just behind the nose, four small fins in a cross at the tail and a short ring-shaped duct around the tail propeller. The body is unbroken along its length with no wings and no straight edges. Not a missile: no cross wings at midbody, no landing gear, no mast.
partPrompts.7: A tracked uncrewed ground vehicle seen three-quarter: a low flat box-shaped chassis carried on two continuous tracks that run the full length of each side over five road wheels, with a short vertical sensor mast rising from one corner of the deck and a small box on top of it. Squat and wide, with the tracks clearly the dominant feature. No turret, no wheels with tires, no wings, no rotors and no boat hull.
